items.title: Compiled Python cache committed to the repository

findings.title: Compiled Python cache committed to the repository
findings.explanation: A 93 KB CPython 3.13 bytecode file is committed. It is not installed by CMake so it does not affect users at runtime, but it is a stale binary artifact that can drift from the source and should not be in the source repository.
findings.suggestion: Remove PETDenoise/__pycache__ and add __pycache__/ and *.pyc to .gitignore.

findings.title: Compiled bytecode committed to the repository
findings.explanation: PETDenoise/__pycache__/PETDenoise.cpython-313.pyc (93 KB) is a build artifact from a developer machine. It is not needed for the extension, may not match the source, and should not be in the source tree.
findings.suggestion: Remove __pycache__ from the repository and add it to .gitignore.

items.title: Denoising and metric computation run on the GUI thread

findings.title: Denoising and metric computation run on the GUI thread
findings.explanation: The whole sliding-window inference (PETDenoise.py lines 1184-1266) and the metric computation (VolumeComparator.py lines 406-464) run in the button-click slot; progress is only shown by pumping the Qt event loop with processEvents. During a long run the UI stays re-entrant, so scene changes or module switches can occur mid-inference, and the application appears frozen between log messages.
findings.suggestion: Move the heavy work to a slicer.util.ProgressDialog / CLI-style worker thread (or a qSlicerCLI-like background task) and keep processEvents out of the compute path.

items.title: Model download silently overwrites a same-named file of different size

findings.title: Model download silently overwrites a same-named file of different size
findings.explanation: isCompleteModelFile returns False for an existing file of a different size, so the download path is taken and os.replace() overwrites the file in the user's model folder. A user-supplied model with the same name, or a partially edited file, is replaced without confirmation. The data loss is limited to model files, but it is unannounced.
findings.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before replacing an existing file, or download into a separate folder and report the conflict.

items.title: Model folder path is written into the extension installation directory

findings.title: Model folder path is written into the extension installation directory
findings.explanation: saveModelFolderPath writes model_config.ini next to the module file. In an installed extension that directory is typically read-only (and shared by all users), so the write fails and is only logged at info level; the setting is still kept in QSettings, so functionality is preserved, but writing into the program installation is not a user-chosen location.
findings.suggestion: Keep the folder only in QSettings, or write the compatibility ini into the user settings/cache directory instead of the module directory.

items.title: Module icon and banner PNGs are not installed by CMake

findings.title: Module icon and banner PNGs are not installed by CMake
findings.explanation: PETDenoise.py lines 282-284 and 376-381 (and VolumeComparator.py lines 32-34, 82-87) load Resources/logo.png and Resources/banner.png, but only Icons/*.png and UI/*.ui are listed as module resources, so those files are not installed with the extension. The os.path.exists guards mean no crash, but users of the installed extension get no module icon and no banner, and the 9 MB banner files are dead weight in the repository.
findings.suggestion: Add Resources/logo.png (and, if wanted, Resources/banner.png) to MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES in both module CMakeLists.txt files, or drop the unused images.

items.title: Registered ctest has no unittest class to run

findings.title: Registered ctest has no unittest class to run
findings.explanation: Both module CMakeLists.txt register a Python unittest on the module script, but a search for unittest classes in PETDenoise.py and VolumeComparator.py found none, and Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt only contains a commented-out line. The generated test therefore exercises nothing, so the extension ships without any automated verification of the denoising or metric code.
findings.suggestion: Add a real test class (e.g. exercising parseSidecar/parseSequence/validateParameters and the metric formulas on synthetic arrays) or remove the test registration.

items.title: Release asset names from GitHub are used as file paths without sanitization

findings.title: Release asset names from GitHub are used as file paths without sanitization
findings.explanation: Asset names come from the GitHub release JSON (parseReleaseAssets, lines 207-221) and are joined directly onto the model folder, both for the .pth (line 1021) and the sidecar (line 1036). An asset named e.g. '../../x.pth' would make the download write outside the chosen model folder. The repository is author-controlled, so the practical risk is low, but the path is not validated.
findings.suggestion: Reject asset names containing path separators or '..' (e.g. require os.path.basename(name) == name) before using them as file names.

items.title: Terms for the downloadable pretrained model weights are not stated

findings.title: License of the downloaded model weights is not stated
findings.evidence:
Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
of this software and associated documentation files (the "SlicerPETDenoise"), to deal
in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights
to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell
findings.explanation: The MIT text covers the extension source; the .pth weights downloaded from the repository's GitHub releases are not explicitly covered by a stated license, and the README does not say under which terms the models may be used or redistributed. This is a clarity gap rather than a prohibition.
findings.suggestion: State in the README (and ideally in the release notes) that the published model weights are released under the same MIT terms or another named license.

findings.title: Terms for the downloadable pretrained model weights are not stated
findings.explanation: The module downloads .pth weights from the GitHub release 'Models' and 'SuperRes_Models'. The repository MIT license covers the code only. Users and redistributors have no stated terms for the weights, so the permission to distribute or use them for any purpose is unclear.
findings.suggestion: State the license or terms for the published models in the release notes or README.

findings.title: Two 9 MB banner images committed
findings.explanation: The scan reports PETDenoise/Resources/banner.png and VolumeComparator/Resources/banner.png at ~9 MB each (not readable here). Large binaries in the source repository slow clones and the extension build, and they are not even installed (see the resource finding).
findings.suggestion: Downscale the banners to a few hundred KB, or reference the images from the README only.

items.title: Unpinned monai install and exact einops pin in Slicer's shared environment

findings.title: Unpinned monai install and exact einops pin in Slicer's shared environment
findings.explanation: After user confirmation, `slicer.util.pip_install("monai")` (also VolumeComparator.py line 309) resolves monai's dependencies inside Slicer's Python, which can upgrade Slicer-bundled numpy, while `einops==0.6.1` is an exact pin that can conflict with other extensions needing a newer einops. Installation is at least user-confirmed and not at import, so this is not a blocking environment change.
findings.suggestion: Pin a tested monai version (e.g. monai==1.3.x) and relax the einops pin to a minimum version, and mention the tested versions in the README.

findings.title: einops pinned to an exact old version in the shared Python environment
findings.explanation: When the user accepts the install prompt, the module runs pip install einops==0.6.1 into Slicer's shared environment. This can downgrade einops for other extensions or conflict with newer packages that need a later version. The prompt does not mention the version downgrade.
findings.suggestion: Use a lower-bound requirement (for example einops>=0.6.1) or document the pin and its reason in the prompt; avoid exact pins in shared environments.

items.title: scm_revision points to a moving branch ('main')

findings.title: scm_revision points to a moving branch ('main')
findings.explanation: The catalog entry pins no commit, so the index builds whatever is on main at build time. The reviewed source (commit 40a63cbf...) can change without any review. This is not a security defect, but it weakens reproducibility and the basis of this review.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to the reviewed commit SHA, or accept that updates need a new review.

items.title: torch.load fallback without weights_only for old PyTorch

findings.title: torch.load fallback without weights_only for old PyTorch
findings.evidence:
# weights_only: a .pth file cannot run arbitrary code when it is loaded
            state = torch.load(modelPath, map_location=device, weights_only=True)
        except TypeError:  # PyTorch < 1.13
            state = torch.load(modelPath, map_location=device)
findings.explanation: On a PyTorch older than 1.13 the code silently falls back to a full pickle load of a user-supplied .pth file, which can execute arbitrary code. The PyTorch extension normally provides a recent build, so this path is unlikely, but it removes the protection exactly where a user-chosen model file is loaded.
findings.suggestion: Drop the fallback and report that a newer PyTorch (from PyTorch Utils) is required, or keep weights_only and fail with a clear message on TypeError.

items.title: Automatic GitHub API request when the download section is opened

findings.title: Automatic GitHub API request when the download section is opened
findings.explanation: Expanding the 'Download Published Models' section contacts api.github.com (at most once per day) without a separate confirmation. Only the request itself (IP address, User-Agent '3DSlicer-PETDenoise') leaves the machine; no image data, identifiers or telemetry are sent, so this is informational.
findings.suggestion: Optionally mention in the README/tooltip that opening the section queries GitHub for the model list.

findings.title: Automatic GitHub API request when the download section is opened
findings.explanation: Opening 'Download Published Models' sends an HTTP request to api.github.com (at most once a day) with a fixed User-Agent. No user data is sent, and the request is not a telemetry channel, but it is network access the user does not explicitly start.
findings.suggestion: Mention the GitHub check in the documentation, or make it manual-only.

items.title: Committed model_config.ini contains the author's local path

findings.title: Committed model_config.ini contains the author's local path
findings.explanation: The committed ini holds a developer machine path. It is harmless to users (loadModelFolderPath only uses it if the directory exists) but it is a leftover development artifact and reveals the author's local layout.
findings.suggestion: Remove model_config.ini from the repository and add it to .gitignore.

findings.title: No automated tests are active
findings.explanation: The module Testing/Python CMake files only contain a commented-out test line, so the generic tests and the unit test are not registered. Changes to the parsing, metric, and sliding-window logic are not covered by automated checks.
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests for parseSidecar, parseSequence, and mergePublishedModelCatalog, which are pure functions.
